Coder brief:
Fix a matching bug in `setPriority(id, priority)` in the default priority queue. p-queue v10.0.0.

File to edit: `source/priority-queue.ts`.

The bug: in `PriorityQueue#setPriority`, the lookup predicate is inverted, so it finds the first live element whose id is NOT the target instead of the element whose id IS the target. This causes `setPriority` to update a different queued task, and causes a missing ID to be silently accepted (mutating a wrong element) instead of throwing.

Exact current code, `source/priority-queue.ts` lines 92–105:
```ts
	setPriority(id: string, priority: number) {
		const index = this.#findIndex(element => element.id !== id);
		if (index === -1) {
			throw new ReferenceError(`No promise function with the id "${id}" exists in the queue.`);
		}

		// Moving it would put it behind the tasks with the same priority.
		if (this.#queue[index]!.priority === priority) {
			return;
		}

		const [item] = this.#queue.splice(index, 1);
		this.enqueue(item!.run, {priority, id});
	}
```

The fix: change the predicate to `element.id === id`:
```ts
		const index = this.#findIndex(element => element.id === id);
```
This is the only code change needed.

Facts showing why the surrounding logic is already correct and no structural change is necessary:
- The queue is a plain JS array kept sorted descending by priority; dequeued slots before `#head` are left as `undefined` and the live range is `#queue[#head] .. #queue[length-1]`.
- `#findIndex` already scans only the live range starting at `#head` (lines 28–37), so ID matching works correctly even after previous dequeues.
- `dequeue()` nulls the head slot and advances `#head` instead of shift/splice (lines 39–56, 120–122); `#compact()` physically splices the consumed prefix when needed (lines 18–26). So consumed entries keep their array indices and are correctly excluded by the `#head`-relative scan.
- The throw for unknown IDs uses `ReferenceError` with the exact message `No promise function with the id "<id>" exists in the queue.` — with the corrected `===` predicate, `#findIndex` returns `-1` for a missing ID and this already-existing throw fires.
- FIFO at equal priority is preserved by `enqueue`: same/lower priority appends to the tail when `this.#queue.at(-1)!.priority! >= priority`, and higher priority uses a binary lower-bound insertion. Do not change `enqueue` or `lowerBound`.

Do NOT change `source/index.ts`. The public `PQueue.setPriority` wrapper (lines 837–852) already validates finite priority and locates the waiting task by strict id equality in its `#waitingTasks` set before delegating; it is correct.

Do NOT touch `test/*`, config files, or `.bench` files — they are immutable.

- Full queue tests: `node --import=tsx/esm --test --test-timeout=60000 test/priority-queue.ts test/validation.ts test/debug.ts test/basic.ts test/advanced.ts`

Expected after fix (these existing tests will now pass):
- `PriorityQueue ignores consumed items with no live match` — after dequeuing `first`, `setPriority('first', 1)` must throw `ReferenceError: No promise function with the id "first" exists in the queue.`

Fix a matching bug in `setPriority(id, priority)` in the default priority queue. p-queue v10.0.0.

File to edit: `source/priority-queue.ts`.

The bug: in `PriorityQueue#setPriority`, the lookup predicate is inverted, so it finds the first live element whose id is NOT the target instead of the element whose id IS the target. This causes `setPriority` to update a different queued task, and causes a missing ID to be silently accepted (mutating a wrong element) instead of throwing.

Exact current code, `source/priority-queue.ts` lines 92–105:
```ts
	setPriority(id: string, priority: number) {
		const index = this.#findIndex(element => element.id !== id);
		if (index === -1) {
			throw new ReferenceError(`No promise function with the id "${id}" exists in the queue.`);
		}

		// Moving it would put it behind the tasks with the same priority.
		if (this.#queue[index]!.priority === priority) {
			return;
		}

		const [item] = this.#queue.splice(index, 1);
		this.enqueue(item!.run, {priority, id});
	}
```

The fix: change the predicate to `element.id === id`:
```ts
		const index = this.#findIndex(element => element.id === id);
```
This is the only code change needed.

Facts showing why the surrounding logic is already correct and no structural change is necessary:
- The queue is a plain JS array kept sorted descending by priority; dequeued slots before `#head` are left as `undefined` and the live range is `#queue[#head] .. #queue[length-1]`.
- `#findIndex` already scans only the live range starting at `#head` (lines 28–37), so ID matching works correctly even after previous dequeues.
- `dequeue()` nulls the head slot and advances `#head` instead of shift/splice (lines 39–56, 120–122); `#compact()` physically splices the consumed prefix when needed (lines 18–26). So consumed entries keep their array indices and are correctly excluded by the `#head`-relative scan.
- The throw for unknown IDs uses `ReferenceError` with the exact message `No promise function with the id "<id>" exists in the queue.` — with the corrected `===` predicate, `#findIndex` returns `-1` for a missing ID and this already-existing throw fires.
- FIFO at equal priority is preserved by `enqueue`: same/lower priority appends to the tail when `this.#queue.at(-1)!.priority! >= priority`, and higher priority uses a binary lower-bound insertion. Do not change `enqueue` or `lowerBound`.

Do NOT change `source/index.ts`. The public `PQueue.setPriority` wrapper (lines 837–852) already validates finite priority and locates the waiting task by strict id equality in its `#waitingTasks` set before delegating; it is correct.
